--- format: revealjs: center: true slide-number: false progress: false code-overflow: wrap theme: [default, custom.scss] --- ::: {style="text-align: center"} ## Asking Sensitive Questions
in the Social Sciences {.center .smaller}   **Gustavo Diaz** Department of Political Science [gustavodiaz.org](https://gustavodiaz.org) [polisci.northwestern.edu](https://polisci.northwestern.edu) ::: ## About me ::: {.cell} ::: ![](misc/diaz_nu_profile.png) ## Why am I a political scientist? ## About you ::: incremental - You will be a Weinberg College major - You will major in political science - You will major in a social science discipline - You plan to conduct research during undergrad - You took AP Math/Calc/Statistics ::: ## Some questions ::: incremental - Have you lied about being sick to skip class or get an extension? - Would you bribe a police officer to avoid a traffic ticket? - Have you used a fake ID to purchase alcohol or cigarettes? - Do you know anyone with ties to a terrorist organization? - Would you allow illegal immigrants to become citizens? ::: ## What do these have in common? ::: incremental - They are **sensitive questions** - We can only learn about them by asking directly - But asking about them directly leads to **misreporting** - This kind of *measurement error* is called **social desirability bias** or **sensitivity bias** ::: ## What can we do? ::: incremental - Honestly appeals - Confidentiality protocols - Indirect questioning techniques ::: ## What can we do? - Honestly appeals - Confidentiality protocols - **Indirect questioning techniques** ## Example ::: {.r-stack} ![](list/personhood_0.png){.fragment width="75%" fig-align="right"} ![](list/personhood_1.png){.fragment} ::: ::: aside Source: [NPR](https://www.npr.org/sections/itsallpolitics/2011/11/08/142159280/mississippi-voters-reject-personhood-amendment) ::: ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **Direct question** . . . Did you vote YES or NO on the Personhood Initiative, which appeared on the November 2011 Mississippi General Election Ballot? . . . $$ \text{Proportion(Voted yes)} =\\ \text{Mean(Answer yes)} $$ ::: aside Source: [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List experiment** Here is a list of things that some people have done. ::: aside Source: [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List experiment** Please listen to them and then tell me HOW MANY of them you have done in the past two years. ::: aside Source: [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List experiment** Do not tell me which ones. Just tell me HOW MANY: . . . ### Control group 1. Discussed politics with family or friends 2. Cast a ballot for governor Phil Bryant 3. Paid dues to a union 4. Given money to a Tea Party candidate ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List experiment** Do not tell me which ones. Just tell me HOW MANY: ### Treatment group 1. Discussed politics with family or friends 2. Cast a ballot for governor Phil Bryant 3. Paid dues to a union 4. Given money to a Tea Party candidate ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List experiment** Do not tell me which ones. Just tell me HOW MANY: ### Treatment group 1. Discussed politics with family or friends 2. Cast a ballot for governor Phil Bryant 3. Paid dues to a union 4. Given money to a Tea Party candidate 5. **Voted "YES" on the Personhood Initiative** ## Post-election survey {{< fa phone >}} **List Experiment Estimation** $$ \text{Proportion(Voted yes)} =\\ \text{Mean(treatment)} - \text{Mean(tontrol)} $$ ## Results ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Results {visibility="uncounted"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Results {visibility="uncounted"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## Results {visibility="uncounted"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Rosenfeld et al (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1111/ajps.12205) ::: ## How does it work? ::: incremental - Respondents are randomly assigned to conditions - Differences in responses can only be attributed to the presence/absence of the sensitive item - So $\text{Mean(treatment)} - \text{Mean(control)}$ gives a *population prevalence rate* - But we **do not know** who they are in our survey! - AND participants **do not know** what we care about! ::: ## Limitations ::: incremental 1. Deception 2. Results depend on baseline list ::: ## Limitations 1. Deception 2. **Results depend on baseline list** --- ![](list/diaz_dle.png){fig-align="center"} --- ::: {.list-table} - - **List A** - **List B** - - Californians for Disability - American Legion - - California National
Organization for Women - Equality California - - American Family Association - Tea Party Patriots - - American Red Cross - Salvation Army ::: . . . **Sensitive item:** Citizen order patrol combating undocumented immigration --- ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Diaz (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1017/XPS.2023.24) ::: --- ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etla_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Diaz (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1017/XPS.2023.24) ::: ## What went wrong? You need to convince yourself two **assumptions** are true . . . ::: {.callout-warning} ### 1. No liars Those who **do not** hold the sensitive item **never** falsely claim to bear it. ::: . . . ::: {.callout-warning} ### 2. No design effects Including the sensitive item **does not change** how participants respond to the baseline items ::: # Other techniques ## Randomized response For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. If {{< fa dice-six >}} shows, tell me *yes*. ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. If {{< fa dice-six >}} shows, tell me *yes*. But if another number shows, tell me your own opinion about the question. . . .   [TURN AWAY FROM PARTICIPANT] . . .   Now you throw the dice so that I cannot see what comes out. ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. If {{< fa dice-six >}} shows, tell me *yes*. But if another number shows, tell me your own opinion about the question.   [TURN AWAY FROM PARTICIPANT]   Have you thrown the dice? ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. If {{< fa dice-six >}} shows, tell me *yes*. But if another number shows, tell me your own opinion about the question.   [TURN AWAY FROM PARTICIPANT]   Have you picked it up? ## Randomized response {visibility="uncounted"} For this question, I want you to answer *yes* or *no*. But I want you to consider the number of your dice throw. If {{< fa dice-one >}} shows on the dice, tell me *no*. If {{< fa dice-six >}} shows, tell me *yes*. But if another number shows, tell me your own opinion about the question.   Now, during the height of the conflict in 2007 and 2008 *(in Afghanistan)*, did you know any militants, like a family member, a friend, or someone you talked to on a regular basis? . . . Please, before you answer, take note of the number you rolled on the dice. ## How does it work? ::: incremental - We know that about $1/6 \approx 0.17$ respondents said *yes* because they rolled a {{< fa dice-six >}} - So if $30\%$ in total said *yes* - We have $\widehat{\text{Prevalence}} = 0.3 - 0.17 = 0.13$ as our *population estimate* - But we **do not know** who they are in our survey! ::: ## Assumptions . . . ::: {.callout-warning} ### 1. Honesty given protection People respond honestly when guaranteed anonymity. ::: . . . ::: {.callout-warning} ### 2. One-sided lying Those who **do not** hold the sensitive trait **never** falsely claim to bear it. ::: ## What is different? ::: incremental - **List experiment:** Bury the lead - **Randomized response:** Emphasize anonymity ::: . . . **Both:** Add *noise* to the question ## Endorsement experiment . . . **Control group** . . . The World Health Organization recently announced a plan to introduce universal polio vaccination across Pakistan. How much do you support such a plan? . . . ::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} (1\) A great deal; (2) A lot; (3) A moderate amount; (4) A little; (5) Not at all. ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Bullock et al (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1093/pan/mpr031) ::: ## Endorsement experiment **Treatment group** The World Health Organization recently announced a plan to introduce universal polio vaccination across Pakistan. How much do you support such a plan? ::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} (1\) A great deal; (2) A lot; (3) A moderate amount; (4) A little; (5) Not at all. ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Bullock et al (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1093/pan/mpr031) ::: ## Endorsement experiment **Treatment group** The World Health Organization recently announced a plan to introduce universal polio vaccination across Pakistan. [_**Pakistani militant groups fighting in Kashmir have voiced support for this program.**_]{style="color: #4E2A84;"} How much do you support such a plan? ::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"} (1\) A great deal; (2) A lot; (3) A moderate amount; (4) A little; (5) Not at all. ::: ::: aside Adapted from [Bullock et al (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1093/pan/mpr031) ::: ## Wisdom of the crowds ![](misc/wisdom.png){fig-align="center" width=50%} ::: aside **URL:** . See [Lehrer et al (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.electstud.2018.09.012) for details ::: ## Takeaways - Sometimes asking weird questions brings you closer to the truth - Crafting survey questions involves extensive trial and error - Extends to any original data collection exercise! ::: {style="text-align: center"} **Thank you!** [gustavodiaz.org](https://gustavodiaz.org) [polisci.northwestern.edu](https://polisci.northwestern.edu)

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
